_meta.purpose: Phase-D2+D3 golden set (BETA campaign) — same architecture as tests/eval/piet_d1 (isolated per-case --do invocations, oracle-verbatim expected values, display-precision tolerances, standalone leg not wired into run_eval.py). D2 wirings are LANDED (op/piet @9ab18ef) — D2 cases gate GREEN against that build. D3 wirings are IN FLIGHT — D3 cases are authored golden-FIRST and are RED against the current build (RED-baseline.txt records that state); they must turn GREEN when the D3 wiring lands.

oracle_logs.d2: internal capture d2-oracle-stata.log (real StataBE 19.5, import delimited fatalities.csv, 336 obs, sections D2a..D2g)
oracle_logs.d2_mediate: internal capture d2b-mediate.log (the ONLY working Stata mediate invocation on this dataset: continuous(0.5 1))
oracle_logs.drdid: <repo>/tests/validate/drdid2x2.log (+ drdid2x2.do for the exact command surface, drdid2x2.dta as the data; full-precision ATT/SE from the log's %20.15g di line)

_meta.dataset_loader: D2 + D3a-g: `sysuse fatalities, clear` (piet's bundled-sample shortcut, byte-identical to the oracle's import-delimited load — established in piet_d1). D3h: `use {DRDID_DTA}, clear` — the driver resolves the {DRDID_DTA} placeholder to tests/validate/drdid2x2.dta (op-eval copy first, then the main worktree copy, env DRDID_DTA override; sha256-identical copies verified 2026-07-15).

tolerance_policy.rationale: Same derivation as piet_d1: oracle values are Stata's DISPLAYED numbers, so each pin's true precision is bounded by its last displayed digit. Worst display-precision cases surveyed across D2/D3: coef/se ~1.3e-4 relative (D2c unemp b=-.007616); scalar chi2 ~2.2e-3 relative (D3b LR chi2=2.25, 2 decimals). Small pseudo-R2 values displayed at 4dp (D3b r2_pseudo=.0017) have display precision up to ~3e-2 RELATIVE but only 5e-5 ABSOLUTE — hence the scalar comparator passes on EITHER rtol OR the 1e-4 atol floor (2x the half-last-digit absolute bound), instead of inflating rtol for everyone. EXCEPTION: d3h_drdid's oracle is FULL float64 precision (%20.15g di line, not display-rounded), so that case tightens to the B3/MI-049 ratified cross-impl tolerance (coef_rel=5e-4) via its per-case tol_override — see the case.
tolerance_policy.integer_fields: EXACT (n_obs, censoring counts, n_selected, tau is float-exact-by-construction but graded as required scalar)

coeftable_name_aliases.__note: Same as piet_d1: the live D2 blocks use '(intercept)' (verified 2026-07-15 on @9ab18ef for tobit/heckman/qreg). The driver tries both spellings.

check_severity_model.coefs / equations[*].coefs: FATAL — missing row or numeric miss fails the case
check_severity_model.required_scalars: FATAL — absent OR mismatched fails (used only where the landed D2 schema is live-verified to carry the field)
check_severity_model.scalars: SECONDARY — absent logs a schema note (non-fatal); present-but-mismatched IS fatal. Used for D3's in-flight schemas where field names are educated guesses (ll/chi2/r2_pseudo/n_groups) — per Art 10, Eval updates the lookup names (never the pinned values) if the landed wiring spells them differently.
check_severity_model.unpinned_oracle_reference: NOT GRADED — oracle values recorded for future use where the landed/expected schema demonstrably lacks the field (e.g. tobit/qreg wirings emit no chi2/r2_pseudo; live-verified) or where the value is degenerate (nbreg boundary alpha).

_meta.d2_schema_provenance: All D2 graded field names live-verified against op/piet @9ab18ef (2026-07-15): tobit block carries ll/variance/se_variance/ul_limit|ll_limit/n_uncensored/n_left_censored/n_right_censored; heckman carries lambda/se_lambda/rho/sigma/n_selected + the reg3-style two-entry 'outcomes' array (depvar inc_obs, high); qreg carries tau/sum_adev/sparsity/bwidth; mediate carries treatment_levels + a/b/direct/indirect/total/se_*/bootstrap{reps,seed,...}.

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: the landed tobit wiring emits no chi2/r2_pseudo fields (live-verified full block dump 2026-07-15)

d2a_tobit_ul.notes: Right-censored tobit at ul(15000) on a depvar constructed to actually hit the limit (min(income,15000) censors 91 obs). variance/se_variance = Stata's var(e.inc_cens) row.

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: same as d2a — no chi2/r2_pseudo in the landed tobit block

d2b_tobit_ll.notes: Left-censored mirror of d2a (ll(11000), 24 obs censored). Together the pair proves ll()/ul() are genuinely independent code paths, not one flag aliased to the other.

d2c2_heckman_twostep_rho_boundary.stata: heckman inc_obs beertax, select(drinkd = spirits unemp) twostep
do_body: heckman inc_obs beertax, select(drinkd = spirits unemp) twostep
d2c2_heckman_twostep_rho_boundary.notes: Boundary-rho regression pin from the 2026-08-01 professor pangram. Stata reports that the unconstrained two-step rho=-1.195376 is truncated to -1 under default rhosigma behavior; sigma is adjusted consistently and the beertax VCE must use the boundary-adjusted values. The old untruncated engine path produced se=332.7821704485568, so this case discriminates the corrected covariance path sharply.

d2d_heckman_mle_reject.stata: heckman inc_obs beertax, select(high = spirits unemp)   [Stata default = full MLE]
do_body: heckman inc_obs beertax, select(high = spirits unemp)

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: Stata's MLE heckman runs fine (oracle D2d, rc=0) but the engine implements ONLY two-step Heckit — PIET honest-rejects the MLE form per the coordinator's gate note rather than silently answering an MLE request with two-step numbers. These oracle MLE values are recorded UNPINNED for a future engine MLE implementation.

d2d_heckman_mle_reject.notes: Honest-reject case: PASS = the run STOPS with the documented unsupported_option error naming the two-step alternative. A future engine heckman-MLE would flip this case's design (reject -> golden with the values above) — that is a deliberate Eval decision at that time, not a tolerance relax.

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: no r2_pseudo in the landed qreg block (live-verified)

d2e_qreg_median.notes: Median regression with NO quantile() option — tau must come back 0.5 via cobra's own --tau default (proves the default path, not just the explicit-quantile path). sum_adev = Stata's 'Min sum of deviations'.

d2f_qreg_p25.notes: quantile(.25) — tau=0.25 required in the block (proves the quantile() forward, distinct from d2e's default). Different b/se from the median case on the same data is itself the estimator-really-moved signal.

d2g_mediate_engine_parity.grading: Run the SAME do_body TWICE (two cold --do invocations, identical fixed seed). PASS iff: (1) both runs complete; (2) block['treatment_levels'] == [0.5, 1.0] (the continuous(#L0 #L1) parse-and-tag proof); (3) block['bootstrap']['reps'] == 199 and block['bootstrap']['seed'] == 20260715 (options genuinely forwarded); (4) the two runs' full estimation blocks are byte-identical under canonical JSON serialization (sort_keys) — fixed-seed reproducibility of the ENTIRE payload including the bootstrap CIs.

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED (coordinator directive): the engine's mediate computes a no-interaction Baron-Kenny per-unit decomposition while Stata's continuous(#L0 #L1) mediate fits a treatment#mediator-interaction model with VanderWeele NDE/NIE at the (0.5,1) contrast — ~20-95% point-estimate divergence, disclosed in [BETA D2]'s commit and in the wiring's own source comment (estimation_m4.cpp runMediate, 'ENGINE-PARITY DISCLOSURE, NOT STATA-PARITY'). Pinning Stata's numbers would hard-RED a documented, disclosed engine-model gap; this case gates what IS promised: deterministic reproducibility + honest option forwarding. If cobra later gains the interaction+contrast model, upgrade this case to golden with these values.

d2g_mediate_engine_parity.notes: The engine block's direct/indirect/total are NOT NDE/NIE/TE — see unpinned_oracle_reference.__why.

d3a_poisson.notes: Pooled Poisson, iid SEs. Scalars are SECONDARY (in-flight schema, field names are the cobraToEstimation passthrough's existing spellings — ll/r2_pseudo/chi2 — as the most likely landing shape).

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: chi2=2.25 (2dp) and r2_pseudo=.0017 (4dp on a tiny value) are the two worst display-precision scalars in the whole leg — recorded but left unpinned to keep the tolerance policy honest; ll is the sharper likelihood pin for the same fit

d3b_poisson_offset.notes: THE defining test is the offset: a wiring that silently drops offset(lpop) still 'runs' but gets b(_cons)=1.94-ish (the no-offset fit) instead of -7.914716 — a >100x coefficient shift, unmissable. Do NOT expect a coeftable row for lpop (Stata shows it as '1 (offset)', display-only).

d3c_poisson_robust.notes: Identical b's to d3a by construction (vcov never moves MLE point estimates) with DIFFERENT robust se's — the parsed-and-ignored-vce trap detector, same pattern as piet_d1's d1c.

d3d_ppmlhdfe_absorb.notes: PPML with one absorbed FE dimension (snum, 48 categories). ppmlhdfe's default vce IS robust (the oracle's SEs are the 'Robust std. err.' column with NO vce() given) — a wiring that returns iid SEs here is wrong even though no vce() appears in the command. Stata reports Residual df=287; not pinned (field name unknowable pre-landing).

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: this fixture's cnt is equidispersed, so NB2 collapses to Poisson at the alpha->0 BOUNDARY: Stata itself reports lnalpha with a MISSING se ('.') and alpha=5.61e-20 (pure numerical noise whose exact value is optimizer-dependent) — pinning either would gate noise, not correctness. The b/se/ll matching Poisson's exactly IS the boundary-case correctness signal.

d3e_nbreg.notes: Boundary-case nbreg: correct behavior is coefs == d3a's Poisson coefs (alpha -> 0). See unpinned reference for why alpha/lnalpha are not pinned.

d3f_xtpoisson_fe.notes: Conditional FE Poisson — NO constant term exists in the conditional likelihood (Stata's own output has no _cons row); forbid_cons asserts the wiring doesn't fabricate one. Panel context comes from the preamble's xtset snum year.

d3g_xtlogit_fe.notes: Conditional FE logit. n_obs=77 EXACT is the sharpest check in the D3 set: Stata drops 37 all-positive/all-negative groups (259 obs) from the conditional likelihood — a wiring that reports n_obs=336 kept the degenerate groups and is wrong even if the coefficients look plausible. No constant (conditional likelihood), same forbid_cons assert as d3f.

d3h_drdid_dripw.stata: drdid Y x1 x2, ivar(id) time(t) treatment(treat) dripw
do_body: drdid Y x1 x2, ivar(id) time(t) treatment(treat) dripw
d3h_drdid_dripw.notes: Doubly-robust DID (dripw = IPW-weighted regression flavor), 2x2 panel, oracle from the SSC drdid package run recorded at FULL float64 precision (%20.15g: ATT=2.05610834185971, SE=.124005088944043) — hence the tighter per-case tol_override (B3/MI-049 ratified cross-impl coef_rel=5e-4) instead of the leg-wide display-precision 1e-3. FIXTURE FORMAT NOTE: the original oracle .dta (<repo>/tests/validate/drdid2x2.dta) is legacy format v114, which the engine's dta reader rejects outright ('unsupported legacy format version 114', live-verified) — the driver therefore resolves {DRDID_DTA} to the in-leg drdid2x2_v118.dta, a bit-identical pandas format conversion of the original (verified column-by-column at conversion, 600x6: id/t/Y/x1/x2/treat); the pinned oracle values apply unchanged. SCHEMA NOTE (open, in-flight): `drdid` currently shares dispatcher.cpp's csdid arm (routes to runCsdid); the landed wiring's coeftable row name for the ATT is unknowable now, so the driver tries the coef_aliases list and, failing that, top-level att/se_att fields (att_fallback). Eval updates the LOOKUP (never the pinned values) if the landed shape differs.
